summary:
This joint resolution constitutes an exercise of Congress's authority under the District of Columbia Home Rule Act to disapprove legislation enacted by the Council of the District of Columbia. Its sole operative provision states that Congress disapproves of the Council's action in enacting the Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 (D.C. Act 24-781).

The mechanism invoked is the congressional review process established under the Home Rule Act, which subjects most acts of the D.C. Council to a period of congressional review before they take permanent effect. The resolution identifies the targeted measure as having been enacted by the Council on January 19, 2023, and transmitted to Congress pursuant to section 602(c)(1) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act on January 26, 2023. Section 602(c)(1) governs the transmittal of D.C. acts and the running of the review period during which Congress may adopt a joint resolution of disapproval; enactment of such a resolution into law (i.e., passage by both chambers and presentment to the President under Article I, Section 7) prevents the disapproved act from taking effect.

The resolution does not amend the United States Code or any named federal statute, does not repeal or modify existing federal law, and contains no authorization of appropriations, appropriation, or sunset provision. It effects no change to federal law directly; its legal consequence is confined to nullifying the identified D.C. enactment under the Home Rule Act's disapproval framework.

The document reflects its procedural posture rather than substantive amendments: it was passed by the House of Representatives on April 19, 2023, and, on April 20, 2023, was received in the Senate, read twice, and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. The resolution is a "Referred in Senate" (RFS) version, indicating it had not yet been enacted at the point reflected in this text.

The resolution sets no effective date, deadline, or condition precedent within its own terms; its efficacy depends entirely on completion of the constitutional and statutory legislative process—Senate passage and presidential approval (or override of a veto)—within the review period specified by the Home Rule Act. The resolution does not recite the substance of the underlying D.C. Act 24-781; it identifies that act only by title, D.C. Act number, enactment date, and transmittal date, and expresses disapproval of the Council's action in the aggregate.
